topics.title: Find coefficient
topics.text:
Let $f(x)=(1+ax)\left(1+a^2x\right)\cdots\left(1+a^nx\right)$. Prove that

$$(1+ax)f(ax) = \left(1+a^{n+1}x\right)f(x).$$Define $A_i$ by $a$, $n$, $i$, known that $f(x)=1+A_1x+A_2x^2+\cdots+A_i x^i+ \cdots A_n x^n$.

Solution



We have $f(ax) = \left(1+a^2x\right)\left(1+a^3x\right)\cdots\left(1+a^{n+1}x\right)$.

Therefore

\begin{eqnarray*}
   (1+ax)f(ax) = (1+ax)\left(1+a^2x\right)\left(1+a^3x\right)\cdots\left(1+a^{n+1}x\right) = \left(1+a^{n+1}x\right)f(x).
  \end{eqnarray*}

Please, everyone helps me!

In a shooting match, $8$ clay targets are arranged in two hanging columns of three each and one column of two.  A marksman must break all $8$ targets according to the following rules:

$(1)$ The marksman first chooses a column.

$(2)$ The marksman must then break the lowest unbroken target in the chosen column.

HintAll that matters is the order in which the marksman selects the columns.
